Error-first recall (US-602): assembleErrorFirstContext wraps store/retrieval.ts's searchFactsBm25/assembleContext (no duplicated BM25/token-budget logic) and guarantees a matching error_solution fact leads the packet regardless of raw BM25 rank vs. other fact kinds -- test-proven with a plain fact that outranks the error fact on BM25 yet the error fact still assembles first; emits memory.error_first_recall for session provenance (US-602 AC-2) only when an error fact actually leads. AGENT 2026-07-20: gate-fix retry. dedupe.ts's group key was naive space-joined string concatenation (`${kind} ${ticketId ?? ''} ${content}`), not injective -- a space landing on a field boundary could collide two distinct (ticketId, content) pairs onto the same key (e.g. ticketId='a', content='b c' vs ticketId='a b', content='c'), silently decaying (permanently hiding from recall) a semantically distinct fact -- confirmed by direct reproduction, a real bug. NO new workspace imports in packages/pipeline/package.json — mirror runPipeline`s PipelinePort pattern (W5-17): local port types, deterministic core, all effects injected.

The coverage manifest enumerates ALL of the imported rule set BY NAME — all 30 anti-slop rules and all 66 validators (R-E3, the name-ALL-of-the-set lesson) — each tagged shadow/advisory/gate per D-014. runOnboard stays pure/deterministic, never authors prose and never imports a model/provider directly (Law 6), so a fake dispatch port yields a fully assertable run with no network (Law 9).

All-or-nothing like runPipeline: on any step`s dispatch error the run throws and returns no partial OnboardRunResult — no health assessment is built from a step that did not complete, and no step-complete event is emitted for it.

tickets.title: Phase-validator runner: real validator runs mint a genuine gate receipt under a distinct verifier identity
acceptance: A phase-gate runner executes the phase's declared validator set (`PHASES[n].validators`, read live off the topology, never frozen) against the project's real on-disk deliverables, and records each validator's name, exitCode and gapCount from the actual run. FR-P1's 'No receipt without a real run' is the bar: a hardcoded or assumed pass fails acceptance.

A clean run mints a gate receipt via `@dokima/validators`' `mintValidatorRunReceipt` (whose FIRST production caller this will be). Reaching it requires two lines of dependency wiring, in scope for this ticket: add `"@dokima/validators": "workspace:*"` to `apps/server/package.json`, and `export * from './phases/index.js';` to `packages/pipeline/src/index.ts` so `PHASES` is importable at all. The receipt carries the input-file content hashes FR-P2 later recomputes, so a silently edited doc invalidates it.

The receipt is minted under a verifier identity DISTINCT from the identity that authored the phase output (Law 5, maker != verifier, mechanical not conventional). A red fixture proves a same-identity mint is refused.

Red fixture first, per docs/TESTING.md's planted-defect harness: a phase whose validator genuinely fails mints NO receipt (not a receipt with a failing exit code recorded as passing), and a phase with no validator run at all has no receipt.

Does NOT mint receipts for model-authored `PipelineRunEvent` output. That path stays a plain hash-chained audit event: the SECURITY_W5 CRITICAL fix removed gate receipts there precisely because no independent validator runs on it, and re-adding them would restore the self-attestation this ticket exists to avoid. A test pins that pipeline-run events remain unanchored.
Full gate green including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`; test counts reported in the commit body.

tickets.title: Phase-advance route: wire decideAdvance so a phase transition is gated by a re-verified receipt
acceptance: A phase-advance route calls `decideAdvance` (packages/pipeline/src/phases/advance.ts) with the real `deps.verifyReceipt` bound to `@dokima/events`' `verifyReceipt`, passing the from-phase's CURRENT `PHASES[n].validators` for the gate receipt and `[]` for a waiver receipt, exactly as AdvanceDeps documents.

An advance with no gate receipt is REFUSED, and the refusal names why. FR-P3's 'the UI states which receipts became stale and why' applies: `AdvanceResult.reasons` reaches the caller intact rather than collapsing to a bare 403 or a boolean.

FR-P2's two-way re-verification demonstrably works end to end: editing a phase deliverable after its gate receipt was minted causes the next advance to be refused with the input-hash mismatch surfaced; adding a validator to the phase's declared set likewise refuses on validator-set drift.

The waiver bypass is honored and bounded: a human-signed waiver receipt permits the advance and is marked `waived`, an agent-signed one is rejected (FR-P2 blocklist), and a clean waiver is still refused on phases 4-5 (FR-G5, `assertWaiverEligible`). tickets.title: Byte-preserving board writes — the conductor rewrites all of plan.json on every status change
acceptance: A conductor board write is byte-identical to the file it replaces, apart from the statuses it intentionally changed. Today `conductor.mjs:371,424` write `JSON.stringify(plan, null, 2) + '\n'`, which against the current 493,140-byte board produces a **2,800-byte divergence**: every ASCII-escaped `\u00a7`/`\u2014` becomes literal UTF-8, plus a trailing newline the file does not have.

A test asserts the round-trip mechanically: read the real `plan.json`, write it back through the conductor's serializer unchanged, and assert the bytes are identical. Proving it by eye or by line count is not sufficient — the defect is invisible in a line-count diff and shows up as ~400 changed lines in review.
Changing one ticket's status produces a diff of only the lines for that status — verified in the test, since an unreviewable board diff is the actual harm.
The fix preserves whatever convention the file already uses rather than imposing one, so a repo whose board is written in literal UTF-8 stays that way.
Full gate green including e2e; test counts in the commit body.

tickets.title: No compile step: packages ship raw TypeScript, so the documented `npx dokima` install path cannot work from a registry
acceptance: FILED 2026-07-30 from live verification. No `build` script exists except `apps/web`; all 12 packages export `./src/index.ts`; `tsconfig.base.json` sets `noEmit: true`. The blocker: `tsx` is an `apps/server` **devDependency** while `cli-entry.mjs` spawns `node_modules/.bin/tsx` at runtime, and every `@dokima/*` dep is `workspace:*` — a registry consumer gets neither, so the shim fails at `spawn`. DEPLOYMENT.md 1's `npx dokima` row is NOT deliverable today. W8-05 closed naming this an honest gap and it was never ticketed.

SHAPE DECIDED 2026-07-30 (founder): bundle into ONE published package, not 13. esbuild inlines `apps/server` + all 12 workspace packages; `better-sqlite3`, `execa`, `fastify`, `google-auth-library` and `zod` stay external and become real `dependencies` of the shipped package (they currently live in three different packages' node_modules). esbuild becomes an EXPLICIT devDependency recorded in docs/TECH_STACK.md — it is already in the tree transitively via vite and tsx, and a phantom dependency must not be relied on.

THE ACTUAL WORK, established by probe on 2026-07-30 rather than by reading: esbuild bundles the whole server cleanly (0 errors, 0 warnings, 411KB) and the bundle then DIES on its first run with `ENOENT ... scandir <bundle-dir>/migrations`. **13 non-test sites resolve assets from `import.meta.url` relative to their own source file**, which in a bundle is the bundle's directory. Every one must resolve through a single bundle-aware asset-root helper. A bundle that builds green and cannot boot is the disconnected-pipeline class this repo caught in W9-06 and W9-11.

The assets those sites reach for must actually ship, enumerated from the probe: `packages/events/migrations/**` and the global-db migrations, `content/experts`, `content/guide`, `content/validators`, and `apps/web/dist` (served as the SPA at `apps/server/src/api/main.ts:60`). SEPARATE AND HARDER: `apps/server/src/api/pipeline/onboard-dispatch-port.ts:45` resolves `packages/loop/src/index.ts` — a TypeScript SOURCE file — at runtime. That cannot work from a bundle at all and needs a redesign, not a path fix; if it grows past a small change, split it into its own ticket rather than smuggling it in here.

PROVEN BY EXECUTION, not by the build exiting 0: the bundled server boots under **plain `node`, no `tsx` on PATH, no TypeScript loader**, and answers `/healthz` with `{"status":"ok","db":true,"ws":true}` — `db:true` is the load-bearing part, since it is what proves the migrations actually resolved. Then, as far as offline allows (C-1, law 9, no live registry calls): `pnpm pack`, inspect the tarball to confirm the assets ship and no `workspace:*` survives, install it into a scratch dir and run the binary.

`dist/` gitignored; `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` 1 corrected — it currently says the repo "has no compile step yet" and defers the registry channel as a follow-up, and this ticket IS that follow-up. Full gate green including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`, counts in the commit body. NOTE: at filing this machine sat at load ~150 from an unrelated Kryptkeeper run, where both suites produce timeout-only failures — verify on a quiet machine per the 2026-07-30 STATUS entry.

tickets.title: trace.spec.ts: the trace e2e never sees its own project card — 2 specs red on a quiet machine
acceptance: FILED 2026-07-30 from a quiet-machine e2e run (load ~10, suite 3.7m): `e2e/trace.spec.ts:54` ("the trace view is honestly empty for a ticket no run has ever touched") and `:73` ("replays a run's events labeled by kind") both fail in the shared `openFreshProject` helper at `trace.spec.ts:49`, on `expect(locator('.project-card').filter({hasText: 'Trace E2E <uuid>'})).toBeVisible()` -> `element(s) not found` after 5000ms. The other 56 specs pass.

NOT a W9-13 regression, and this was established rather than assumed: this session's FIRST e2e run, against unmodified `main` before any code change, failed the same two specs with a byte-identical signature — same locator shape, same helper line, differing only in the random project UUID. W9-13 took the suite from 30 failures to 2; these are the 2 that were always there.

ROOT-CAUSED 2026-07-30, and it is NOT what this ticket first guessed. The `computeProjectStats open failed ... directory does not exist` line is a RED HERRING: it appears on a fully green run too, since tests legitimately delete their own tmp dirs. The real cause is that `playwright.config.ts` points `DOKIMA_HOME` at a FIXED tmp path shared by every test AND every run, with `reuseExistingServer` locally, so the Fleet registry is never cleaned. It had reached **1,164 projects / 422KB of fleet.json**, accumulating since 2026-07-23.

PROVEN by wiping that home and re-running the identical suite: **58/58 passed in 22.0s**, against 2 failed in 3.7m immediately before — a 10x wall-clock difference and the failures gone. So the product is not defective and the assertion is not too tight; the harness is not hermetic. The fix therefore belongs in the e2e setup, NOT in trace.spec.ts (whose assertion was correct all along) and NOT in a widened timeout. `GET /api/v1/projects` was separately timed at 286ms with all 1,164 registered, which rules out server latency and points at client-side render volume.

The suite starts from a clean DOKIMA_HOME every run, via Playwright globalSetup, so this cannot silently re-accumulate. Verified the hard way: restore the real 1,164-project fleet.json, then run the full suite and watch it pass anyway — a fix that only works from an already-clean home has not fixed anything.
Full gate green including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`; counts in the commit body.
tickets.notes: FILED 2026-07-30 by the W9-13 session, deliberately as a separate ticket rather than folded into it: W9-13 was a packaging change and these two specs were red before it started. Filing it separately keeps that boundary auditable instead of letting a packaging commit quietly absorb an unrelated UI defect. AMENDED 2026-07-30 mid-implementation: write_scope widened to add apps/web/playwright.config.ts and apps/web/e2e/** because the fix lives in the harness, not in the spec or the app -- the original scope (trace.spec.ts + src/**) could not hold it. DONE 2026-07-30. Fix is a Playwright globalSetup that clears DOKIMA_HOME + the state DB (and its -wal/-shm siblings) before every run, plus e2e/env-paths.ts shared by the config and the setup so the two cannot drift onto different directories — a stale copy in one would silently clear a directory nobody uses. trace.spec.ts was NOT touched: its assertion was correct all along, and widening the timeout would have hidden a real 10x slowdown. tickets.title: Fleet has no way to remove a project, so an entry whose directory is gone is permanent
acceptance: FILED 2026-07-30 out of W9-14, deliberately as a product ticket rather than folded into that test fix. There is no remove/forget/unregister path for a project: grepping `apps/server/src/api/projects.ts` and `apps/web/src/fleet/**` finds no DELETE route and no UI affordance. A project registered once stays in `fleet.json` forever, including after its directory is deleted.

This is not hypothetical and W9-14 measured the consequence. The e2e registry reached **1,164 entries**, almost all pointing at deleted tmp directories, and the Fleet view degraded badly enough that a newly-onboarded project card did not render inside 5s — while `GET /api/v1/projects` itself still answered in 286ms. The server is fine; the accumulated list is what hurts, and a real user hits the same shape more slowly by onboarding, moving, and deleting repos over months.

Decide and record the intended behaviour before building, because two reasonable products differ here: (a) an explicit "Remove from Fleet" action that forgets the registry entry without touching the project on disk, and/or (b) rendering an entry whose directory is missing as a distinct "unavailable" state with a remove affordance, rather than as an ordinary card whose stats silently read zero. Removing a project from the Fleet must never delete the user's repo or its `.dokima/state.db` — that is the sharp edge in this ticket.

Whatever is chosen, the honest-absence rule applies (the same one `healthz` and the trace view already follow): a project whose directory has vanished must not be shown as a healthy card with zeroed stats, since that is indistinguishable from a real, empty project.

Red fixture: a registry containing an entry whose directory does not exist renders the unavailable state (not a zeroed normal card), and removing it leaves the on-disk directory of a still-present project untouched — asserted against the filesystem, not just the API response.
Full gate green including `pnpm --filter @dokima/web e2e`; counts in the commit body.
tickets.notes: FILED 2026-07-30 by the W9-14 session. W9-14 fixed the TEST harness so runs stop accumulating; this ticket is the PRODUCT question that accumulation exposed, and the two were kept separate on purpose — "prune entries whose directory is missing" would have been a product behaviour change smuggled in as a test fix.

tickets.title: One-command autorun — and stop the supervisor destroying uncommitted work on launch
acceptance: Launching unattended currently means hand-typing four lines from CONDUCTOR_RUNBOOK.md (`nohup caffeinate -dimsu bash scripts/supervise.sh ... >> docs/work/conductor.out 2>&1 &` plus a manual pid write). Three of the four fail SILENTLY when forgotten: no caffeinate and the machine sleeps mid-run, no redirect and an overnight run has no log, no pid file and `stop` becomes pkill guesswork against a tree that includes agent sessions. `scripts/autorun.sh start|stop|status` wraps it, passing extra args (`--waves`, `--no-merge`, `--breakpoint`) through to supervise.sh unchanged.

DEFECT FOUND WHILE BUILDING THIS, and it is the more important half of the ticket. `supervise.sh` runs `git checkout -f main` + `git clean -fd` at the TOP OF ITS LAUNCH LOOP — so on every start, not only after a crash, despite the comment describing it as crash recovery. Launching from a feature branch with uncommitted work therefore destroys that work silently. Reproduced by accident, on this ticket: the first `autorun.sh start --lint` discarded W9-16's own uncommitted board filing and deleted the untracked `scripts/autorun.sh` outright.

Same class as the 2026-07-28 fix that stopped this cleanup deleting unmerged BRANCHES — that one protected committed work on branches and left uncommitted and untracked work unprotected. The first launch of a run is a deliberate human act, not crash debris: supervise.sh must REFUSE to start when the tree is dirty or the checkout is not on main, naming what it would have destroyed. Crash-RESTARTS (iteration 2+) keep resetting exactly as today, because there the dirty tree genuinely is a dead attempt's debris.

`autorun.sh start` performs the same check up front so the refusal arrives before anything is backgrounded, and a stale pid file (rebooted machine, SIGKILLed supervisor) never permanently blocks a relaunch — liveness is `kill -0`, not the file's existence.

NOT escalated by default: conductor.config.json $modelsNote records "Overnight runs launch WITHOUT --escalate: sonnet-only ladder, frontier spend requires a human (D-018)". A convenience wrapper that quietly raises the spend ceiling is not a convenience. caffeinate is macOS-only and its absence degrades to running without it (W3-15 portability precedent), never aborts.

Verified WITHOUT spending provider tokens: launch through the wrapper with `--lint` (conductor exits immediately), asserting pid file written, log appended, process reaped, and `status` honest before and after. Separately assert the dirty-tree refusal by launching with a deliberately uncommitted file present and confirming the file SURVIVES. Runbook Launch/Control sections lead with the wrapper, raw incantation kept beneath as the escape hatch.
tickets.notes: FILED 2026-07-30 at Brad's request ("can you do that for this product as well so we can just auto run"). Dokima is where conductor.mjs and supervise.sh were BUILT and from which Kryptkeeper vendored them, so the harness was always here — only the front door was missing. The destroy-uncommitted-work defect was found the hard way, by this ticket losing its own first draft to it, which is the most direct possible evidence for why the guard belongs in the tool rather than in the runbook. DONE 2026-07-30. scripts/autorun.sh start|stop|status + pnpm autorun/autorun:stop/autorun:status. Both layers guarded: autorun refuses before backgrounding anything (so the refusal is on your terminal, not buried in a log you have to go read), and supervise.sh refuses independently for anyone calling it directly. Verified without spending a token: --lint launch writes the pid, appends the log, is reaped, and status reports honestly before and after; a deliberately untracked CANARY.txt SURVIVED both an autorun start and a direct supervise.sh call that would previously have deleted it. Board unchanged throughout. Runbook Launch/Control now lead with the wrapper, raw incantation kept beneath.

tickets.title: Persisted provider registry — a provider you can add without editing JSON by hand
acceptance: TODAY there is no registry: `apps/server/src/cli/ops/providers-core.ts` says so verbatim — "There is no persisted provider registry yet anywhere in the codebase" — and reads a `providers` key out of the three-scope settings file, consumed ONLY by `shipwright doctor` and `providers refresh`. There is no REST surface and no GUI, so registering a provider means hand-editing JSON. Promote it to a real registry with GET/PUT/DELETE under /api/v1/providers, reusing `buildProvider`'s existing kind->adapter switch (ollama | lm-studio | oai-compat | anthropic | openai | vertex) rather than inventing a second one.

Credentials are keychain refs ONLY (Law 8, FR-S2, D-012). Every registry write appends a `settings.changed` event (FR-S3), same discipline as the model matrix (see `settings-events.ts`). RED FIXTURE: a write that skips the event fails the test.

PREREQUISITE, in scope on purpose: `packages/gateway/package.json`'s export map publishes only `./src/index.ts`, and that is the STATED reason `harbormaster/src/loop-land-policy.ts` reimplements escalation policy locally rather than importing it. Widen the map here, or this seam gets reimplemented a fourth time.

tickets.title: Model catalog + discovery — surface the models listModels() already finds
acceptance: Discovery ALREADY EXISTS and is thrown away: the `Provider` contract carries `listModels()`, and `apps/server/src/cli/ops/providers-refresh.ts` calls it — then keeps `modelCount` and DISCARDS the list. Persist the list per provider and expose it. This is a plumbing ticket, not a build-discovery ticket; size it accordingly.

Law 9 / C-1 is the design constraint, not a nice-to-have: opencode's 75-provider list comes from the remote models.dev registry, and first run here must work with ZERO network. Ship a bundled static catalog under `content/model-catalog/` (versioned and provenance-headed like the rest of `content/`), with live `/v1/models` discovery layered on top for any reachable endpoint. A remote registry may be optional; it may never be required.

RED FIXTURE: with no network and no reachable endpoint, the catalog still resolves and the provider is reported UNREACHABLE with the reason — never silently empty, never a fabricated model list (the honest-absence rule W9-15 applied to the Fleet).

Recorded fixtures only, never a live call in a test (Law 9). Contract-test the `/v1/models` shape against recorded LM Studio and Ollama responses, the same discipline `packages/gateway/src/providers/*-fixtures.ts` already uses.
Full gate green including e2e; counts in the commit body.
tickets.notes: W10 Phase G. Sizing note from the plan: because listModels() and providers refresh already exist, the work is exposing what is there plus the offline catalog — NOT building discovery. SCOPE WIDENED 2026-08-02 (schema fix, not a workaround): the original write_scope was packages/gateway/src/catalog/** + content/model-catalog/** only, which made the ticket UNSATISFIABLE — its own acceptance criterion 1 names apps/server/src/cli/ops/providers-refresh.ts as the file that must stop discarding the list, and surfacing the catalog needs the gateway barrel. tickets.title: Wire the seam: the model the user picks is the model that runs
acceptance: THE DEFECT, stated exactly: the only production model-call path in the product is `gateway-model-port.ts` (and its twin `onboard-dispatch-port.ts`), and both build a hardcoded `createOaiCompatProvider` from THREE ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES — `resolveGatewayConfigFromEnv` returns `{baseUrl: DOKIMA_MODEL_BASE_URL ?? 'http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1', apiKey, model: DOKIMA_MODEL_ID ?? 'local-model'}`. Neither call site imports the router, `resolveModelChain`, the matrix, or the registry. The Anthropic, OpenAI-native, Copilot and Vertex adapters are therefore NEVER CONSTRUCTED on any production path — only by their own tests. Resolve provider + model through the registry (W10-01) and the role matrix instead.

THE RED FIXTURE IS THE WHOLE ACCEPTANCE, and it is the W9-11 mutation applied to the bug it would have caught: set the matrix to provider B, assert the call goes to B — then revert ONLY the resolution call site and confirm the test REDS. A test that stays green when the wire is cut is the exact defect this ticket exists to fix, and it must be demonstrated, not asserted.

The matrix is currently read by `roster-resolve.ts` for DISPLAY only ("which model would this role use?"). After this ticket, display and dispatch must agree by construction — resolve once, use for both — so the roster can never advertise a model the pipeline will not call.
Environment variables survive as a documented override for CI and fixtures, and lose to an explicit registry/matrix selection. RED FIXTURE pins the precedence in both directions.

Law 5 / C-4 is preserved mechanically: `guardMakerVerifierDistinct` still refuses a verifier role landing on the maker model through the NEW path. RED FIXTURE proves the guard fires post-wiring — it must not become bypassable by going through the registry.
Full gate green including e2e; counts in the commit body.

Register/edit/test an endpoint (Ollama, LM Studio, any OpenAI-compatible, plus the cloud adapters), see the discovered models from W10-02, and select per role x task-type from a LIST.

Built against the UX_SPEC section W10-05 writes — not invented while building. Covers the states that spec names: empty, unreachable-endpoint, and the maker!=verifier refusal explained INLINE with its reason (the "drag-refusals explained" precedent from the board, FR-C).

An API-key field writes to the keychain and persists a REF, never a literal (Law 8). RED FIXTURE: the value never appears in any settings file or event-log payload, asserted by reading the persisted bytes back.

acceptance: MEASURED STARTING POINT (2026-08-02): FIVE tokens exist — `--sw-bg`, `--sw-fg`, `--sw-border`, `--sw-accent`, `--sw-transition-duration`. There is NO spacing, type, or radius scale (13 distinct ad-hoc px values), and **66 hardcoded hex colours**, of which **54 sit in feature CSS** outside `styles.css` — so they cannot respond to the `data-theme` flip at all. tickets.title: The receipts fetch double-prefixes /api/v1 — the drawer 404s and the palette fails silently
acceptance: OBSERVED 2026-08-02 against the real running product, in BOTH themes: opening any ticket drawer fires GET /api/v1/api/v1/projects/<id>/receipts?ticket=<id> — note the DOUBLED path segment — which 404s. The Receipts section then renders the raw string "Artifact API request failed with status 404" to the end user. Screenshot evidence captured at 1440x900.

ROOT CAUSE, already traced: `request()` in apps/web/src/artifacts/api.ts:49 builds `${opts.baseUrl ?? ''}${urlPath}`, but every urlPath in that module already hardcodes the /api/v1 prefix (e.g. line 179). ArtifactViewerRoot.tsx:69 works because it passes `{ getToken }` with NO baseUrl; EvidencePanel.tsx:30 passes `{ baseUrl, getToken }` where baseUrl is "/api/v1" (App.tsx:343/359/368), so it doubles.

BLAST RADIUS is four call sites in two components, not one: EvidencePanel.tsx:30 (fetchReceipts) plus CommandPalette.tsx:86 (fetchArtifactList), :87 (fetchReceipts) and :142 (fetchReceipt). The palette calls have NO .catch, so they reject unhandled and the palette silently shows no docs and no receipts — a silent failure, strictly worse than the drawer's visible error. Fix all four.

Make the class of bug impossible rather than patching four call sites: either have `request()` reject/normalise a baseUrl that would duplicate the prefix it already carries, or strip the hardcoded prefix from the module and require baseUrl. Pick one and make the other shape a type or runtime error — a third caller will otherwise reintroduce this.

RED FIXTURE, and it is the point: assert the REQUEST URL, not just the parsed response. The reason 2923 tests and 59 e2e specs all pass while this ships broken is that EvidencePanel.test.tsx never asserts a URL and CommandPalette.tsx has NO test file at all. Add a test that fails on a doubled /api/v1 — verified by reverting the fix and confirming red.
Full gate green including e2e; counts in the commit body.
tickets.notes: Found 2026-08-02 by an end-user visual verification sweep (46 screenshots, both themes, real server + real event log) rather than by any test — the capture harness recorded console errors and HTTP >=400 per state, which is what surfaced it. tickets.title: Anchors have no colour rule at all — 1.95:1 in dark — and the design gate is blind to it
acceptance: MEASURED: no `a` colour selector exists in ANY apps/web/src/**/*.css, nor in the built dist CSS. Anchors therefore fall back to the user-agent default #0000EE, measured at 1.95:1 against the dark card background (WCAG AA text needs 4.5:1). Light measures 8.59:1, so this is dark-only. THE GATE HOLE IS THE REAL DELIVERABLE, not the link colour. W10-06 added styles.test.ts, which fails on a raw hex PRESENT in a stylesheet. It cannot see a colour that is NEVER DECLARED — there is no hex for the walker to find. That is exactly how this seventh AA failure survived a ticket whose headline was "six AA failures fixed". Add a check that catches MISSING declarations, not just stray ones: assert every interactive/text role the app renders resolves to a declared --sw-* colour, or assert computed contrast on rendered elements.
RED FIXTURE: remove the new anchor colour rule and confirm the new test goes red. A gate that cannot be made to fail is not a gate (docs/TESTING.md §6).

Scope honesty carried from the audit: one instance was photographed and measured; the root cause is verified global; artifacts/MarkdownView.tsx:42 links are code-traced only and were never seen rendered. Fix globally, but do not claim verification you did not do.

tickets.title: The capture harness can silently shoot a stale build, and its coverage has holes
acceptance: THE HARNESS CAN CAPTURE CODE THAT IS NOT ON MAIN. `ensureSpaBuilt()` in apps/web/scripts/lib/app-harness.mjs returns early whenever dist/index.html merely EXISTS — it never checks whether the bundle is older than the source. A dist left from an earlier commit is then served by the real server and photographed as if it were current. Proven 2026-08-03: a capture run against a 19:18 dist reported the W10-29 receipts fix as still broken (404s, doubled /api/v1); rebuilding and re-running showed 200s and zero console errors. The fix was fine; the harness lied. Make it rebuild unconditionally, or compare mtimes against src/ and fail loudly on staleness. Both capture-tour.mjs and capture-acceptance.mjs depend on this, so docs/tour/ is only as trustworthy as this check.

TWO CAPTURED STATES ARE MIS-SLUGGED, which is worse than missing because they look like coverage: dark/01-fleet-empty.png actually renders a project card, and dark/04-workspace-empty.png renders a seeded board. Assert that a state named "empty" is empty.

Settings has TWELVE tabs, not the five captured. Effective Settings, MCP Servers, Expert Overrides, Rule Lifecycle, Suppressions and Escalation Policy are unverified in both themes. Decisions, Estimate and Lessons never rendered content and the command palette never opened, so their empty and no-query states are unverified too.

Make the capture assert its own denominator: a declared state list it walks, with a failure when a state is skipped or when a captured state does not match what it claims to be. A sweep that cannot report its own coverage cannot sign off UX_SPEC §2b.

docs/tour/img/ is stale on main independently of the above: the shipped captures predate the Dokima rename (headers still read "Shipwright") and 05-board-seeded.png shows the pre-W10-06 six-across clipped layout the code no longer produces. Regenerate once the harness is trustworthy.
Full gate green; counts in the commit body.

tickets.title: The tour fixture fabricates at least two event payload fields production never emits
acceptance: MEASURED 2026-08-03, TWO confirmed fabrications in apps/web/scripts/seed-tour-trace.mjs. (1) Line 39 appends a gate event with payload { validators: [{ name, exitCode, gapCount }] } — mintReceipt (packages/events/src/receipts.ts:363-372) is the SOLE appender of gate.receipt_minted / gate.waived and anchors them with { receiptId, kind, contentMac }; validator results live in the separate `receipts` table. (2) The escalation event carries payload.reason — but EscalationEvent (packages/gateway/src/escalation/events.ts:13-24) declares type, ticketId, fromRung, toRung, actorId, receipts, receiptId?, occurredAt and NO reason field. fromRung/toRung are real; reason is not.

THE HARM IS A FALSE CONTRACT, NOT A WRONG SCREENSHOT. Both fabrications propagated: a visual audit read the fixture, concluded the data existed, tickets were written demanding both be surfaced, and one was implemented before an independent reviewer caught the validators case. The reason case was caught only because the implementing agent checked the emitter itself. Law 9 requires recorded fixtures over live calls; it does not license a fixture to invent a shape the recorder never produced.

Correct the fixture so every appended event carries only what its real appender writes. Where the tour needs richer content, seed through the real seam (mintReceipt, the receipts table, the escalation emitter) instead of hand-authoring a payload. Note that EscalationEvent already carries `receipts` — real triggering evidence the trace could show instead of an invented reason string.

RED FIXTURE: a test that fails when a seeded event payload carries a key its production appender does not write. Derive the expected shape from the emitter/type, not from a hand-maintained list, or it rots the moment a payload changes.
Audit apps/web/e2e/fixtures/** the same way and report findings — seed-board-tickets.mjs backs the e2e suite AND the a11y gate, so a fabricated shape there is load-bearing for far more than the tour.
Record the rule in docs/TESTING.md: a fixture may record LESS than production, never more, and never a differently-shaped payload. Full gate green; counts in the commit body.
